scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Your AC makes the room cold. But stand next to the outdoor unit, and it's blowing hot air. Why?

scenes.name: move
scenes.text: An AC doesn't create cold. It pulls heat out of your room, and dumps it outside.

scenes.name: indoor
scenes.text: Room air is blown across cold coils, where refrigerant evaporates, and soaks up the heat.

scenes.name: dry
scenes.text: Moisture from the air condenses on those cold coils. That's the water dripping from the pipe.

scenes.name: outdoor
scenes.text: The compressor squeezes the refrigerant until it's hot, and the outdoor fan blows that heat away.

scenes.name: inverter
scenes.text: An inverter AC changes its compressor speed, instead of switching fully on and off, so it uses less power.

scenes.name: temp
scenes.text: Every degree lower costs more electricity. That's why India's energy efficiency bureau made twenty four degrees the default.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Absorb, squeeze, release, repeat. Cool, by moving heat. Follow for more on how things really work.
